notes_for_human: DIRECT ANSWER ON UNDERGRADUATE AVAILABILITY: Latham & Watkins' Summer Associate Program is NOT open to undergraduates. It is restricted to enrolled JD candidates at ABA-accredited law schools. Firm's own words (lwcareers.com, tier 1): "The application process is open to all Class of 2029 law students enrolled in an ABA-accredited law school..." and "We offer opportunities for law students at ABA-accredited schools to learn from some of the best in the profession, refine their skills, and develop their talents." A law school transcript is a mandatory application item, which an undergraduate cannot produce. The only mention of an undergraduate transcript is as a SUPPLEMENT for IP Litigation applicants who are already law students. So the common undergraduate belief that a "big law summer program" is open to them is wrong in Latham's case. HOWEVER — and this is the genuinely useful finding for an undergraduate database — Latham does run one undergraduate-facing program on its own domain: the Business Services Training Program (BSTP), "a highly selective rotational program for recent university graduates" in Chicago, Los Angeles (GSO), New York, Washington D.C., London, and Manchester. Two important caveats: (1) it is a full-time post-graduation job of roughly two years, NOT a summer internship, and (2) it is a business-services (non-lawyer) role in finance, business development, attorney support, and technology. The Los Angeles and Manchester tracks are explicitly aimed away from future law students: "Our Los Angeles and Manchester BSTP program is specifically designed for individuals interested in long-term careers in the business of law, rather than those planning to attend law school." The single BSTP variant open to CURRENTLY ENROLLED undergraduates is the London Placement: "A one-year program designed for current university students completing a year-in-industry between their second and final years." BSTP applications open Autumn 2026; there is currently only a register-interest form, no live application. PARALEGAL: Latham hires paralegals as full-time staff requiring a bachelor's degree already completed ("Bachelor's degree required", Paralegal I job description PDF on lw.com). No paralegal internship or undergraduate paralegal pipeline program is published. 1L FELLOWSHIP: I could not verify current eligibility from any tier-1 or reachable tier-2 source. lw.com/1LFellowship no longer serves fellowship content and the University of Texas Law page is 404. Search-engine summaries describe a 10-week 1L program at roughly $3,470/week with a client secondment, but I refused to place any of that in a quote field because I could not open a live page containing that text; treat those figures as unconfirmed. The only live firm-domain confirmation that a 1L track exists is "Our 2026 1L and 2027 2L applications are closed." COMPENSATION AND SPONSORSHIP are silent across every page I read; the summer program page links to a separate "Compensation & Benefits" section I did not open within budget. That section (https://www.lwcareers.com/en/beginning-your-legal-career/united-states/compensation-benefits, path inferred, unverified) is the obvious next fetch. COOLING-OFF is silent everywhere — no reapplication restriction, attempt limit, or waiting period is published for any Latham program. METHOD NOTE: all tier-1 quotes were taken from raw HTML/PDF fetched via curl and text-extracted locally, not from a summarizing fetch tool, specifically to guarantee they are character-for-character.
